 OP (MAC) NO. 100 OF 2025  3  2025:KER:73976  JUDGMENT
Despite service of notice, none appears for the respondent.

2. The petitioner is the applicant in O.P.(MV) No.186 of 2019 before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Attingal, filed claiming compensation for the injury sustained in a motor accident on 06.11.2018.
The claim was originally made under Section 163(A) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short 'MV Act').
Thereafter, the petitioner amended the O.P. (MV) from Section 163(A) to 166(1) and 140 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

Thereafter, the petitioner filed I.A. No.4 of 2025 seeking to amend the claim petition to convert under Section 164 of the MV Act, which has been brought into force with effect from 01.09.2019 as per Act 32 of 2019.

Through Ext.P3 order, the tribunal dismissed the application, holding that Act 32 of 2019, by which Section 164 was brought into force, came on 01.09.2019 and the same does not have any retrospective effect.

3. Challenging the above, the learned Counsel for the petitioner argues that the view taken by the tribunal is contrary to the decisions of the Supreme Court in Rathi Menon v. Union of India (2001 OP (MAC) NO. 100 OF 2025 2025:KER:73976 (3) SCC 714), New India Assurance Co. Ltd v. Urmila Halder ( 2025 ACJ 244), and also Ram Murti and others v. Punjab State Electricity Board (2023 ACJ 631).

sentences.text: The learned Counsel for the petitioner argues based on the judgments of the Supreme Court that all of them, in one voice, held that the amendment made to a beneficial registration ought to be given retrospectivity and the claimants granted the corresponding benefits.

The learned Counsel for the petitioner further submits that the judgment of the learned Single Judge of this Court did not consider the judgments of the Supreme Court on the issue, and therefore, the same must be treated as per incuriam.
5. Ext.P3 order does not reveal consideration of any of the above judgments, possibly because they were not argued before the Tribunal.

However, taking note of the fact that there is no appearance OP (MAC) NO. 100 OF 2025 2025:KER:73976 for the respondent and the Tribunal, in the first instance, can decide the question of law raised by the petitioner, I am inclined to direct a reconsideration of the issue by the Tribunal.
6. Accordingly, Ext.P3 order is set aside.

There will be a direction to the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Attingal, to reconsider I.A. No.4 of 2025 and pass appropriate orders, in accordance with law, within two months from the date of receipt of a copy of the judgment.
It is made clear that all the contentions of the parties are left open.
The original petition is allowed as above.
